<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "Several generic declarations use the token LocalDef008 as a universe-level name, whereas D008 uses it as a real-valued model projection. These are different syntactic roles; the universe occurrences do not refer to the error parameter.",
    "External declarations are supplied only to the stated frontier. In particular, Fin.foldl delegates to an unexpanded private loop. Its standard meaning is an increasing-index left fold; the loop implementation itself is not available for independent inspection here.",
    "The model specifies real-valued operations satisfying error axioms, without specifying a floating-point format, rounding rule, representable subset, or treatment of overflow and underflow."
  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the computed dot product whose absolute error is bounded.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, natural numbers t, B, N, equality hN: B^t = N, and functions x,y: Fin N → ℝ, form v(i) = fl_mul(x(cast hN i), y(cast hN i)) for i ∈ Fin(B^t), and return the recursive sum S(fp,B,t,v) defined in D005.",
      "name": "Computed hierarchical dot product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target universally quantifies over this type, so all the data and axioms specified by its constructor are implicit model assumptions.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "The type of arithmetic models. Its supplied constructor D007 packages a nonnegative real error parameter, five real-valued arithmetic operations, exact addition from a zero accumulator, and relative-error axioms.",
      "name": "Arithmetic model type",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the bound's coefficient at n = t(B−1)+1.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, define γ_n = ((n:ℝ)u)/(1−(n:ℝ)u), where u is the model's error parameter. This is a total real expression in Lean; division by zero has value zero, although the target's hypothesis ensures a positive denominator.",
      "name": "Accumulated error coefficient",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target assumes this predicate at n = t(B−1)+1, ensuring the coefficient's denominator is positive.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, the admissibility predicate is (n:ℝ)u < 1.",
      "name": "Error-budget admissibility",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the grouping and summation algorithm used after the individual rounded products.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and B,t ∈ ℕ, S(fp,B,t,·) maps real vectors of length B^t to ℝ. Its equations are S(fp,B,0,v)=v(0), and S(fp,B,t+1,v)=A(fp,B,j ↦ S(fp,B,t,i ↦ v(j·B^t+i))), where j ∈ Fin B, i ∈ Fin(B^t), and A is D012. Thus it recursively sums B contiguous blocks of length B^t and sequentially adds their results. The definition permits B=0 and t=0.",
      "name": "Recursive B-ary block summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the one rounded multiplication for each input pair.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, selects its fifth field, fl_mul: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ. D007 requires that for all real a,b there exists δ with |δ|≤u and fl_mul(a,b)=ab(1+δ).",
      "name": "Model multiplication projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies all assumptions carried by fp. Addition, multiplication, nonnegativity of u, and exact zero-start addition govern the target algorithm; subtraction, division, and square root are additional model requirements even though the algorithm does not call them.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "Constructs a model from u∈ℝ with 0≤u; operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div: ℝ×ℝ→ℝ and fl_sqrt: ℝ→ℝ; the axiom ∀a∈ℝ, fl_add(0,a)=a; and the following axioms. For every a,b∈ℝ, each of fl_add(a,b), fl_sub(a,b), and fl_mul(a,b) equals, respectively, (a+b)(1+δ), (a−b)(1+δ), and ab(1+δ), for an existential real δ satisfying |δ|≤u. For every a,b∈ℝ with b≠0, fl_div(a,b)=(a/b)(1+δ) for such a δ. For every a∈ℝ with a≥0, fl_sqrt(a)=sqrt(a)(1+δ) for such a δ. Each existential δ may depend on the operation and operands; a common δ is not required. The operations are total, but division at zero and square root at negative arguments have no corresponding error axiom.",
      "name": "Arithmetic model constructor and axioms",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Determines both the admissibility condition and γ_n.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, selects its first field u∈ℝ, whose nonnegativity is included in the model.",
      "name": "Error parameter projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Justifies accessing index zero in the depth-zero summation case.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For every B∈ℕ, 0<B^0. In particular, B^0=1 even when B=0.",
      "name": "Base-level index validity",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes each contiguous-block access in the recursive algorithm well-defined.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For all B,t∈ℕ, j∈Fin B, and i∈Fin(B^t), the natural number j.val·B^t+i.val is strictly less than B^(t+1).",
      "name": "Block index bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the dependent split between depth zero and positive depth in D005; it adds no mathematical hypothesis.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For any B∈ℕ and universe-polymorphic family P(k,v) indexed by k∈ℕ and v:Fin(B^k)→ℝ, given x∈ℕ, v:Fin(B^x)→ℝ, a value h0(w):P(0,w) for every w:Fin(B^0)→ℝ, and a value hs(t,w):P(t+1,w) for every t∈ℕ and w:Fin(B^(t+1))→ℝ, returns P(x,v) by natural-number case analysis. At zero it returns h0(v), and at t+1 it returns hs(t,v). No induction hypothesis is supplied to hs.",
      "name": "Dependent depth case split",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies the sequential addition of the B child results at every internal node. Exact fl_add(0,a)=a makes the first addition exact, leaving at most B−1 nontrivial addition errors per level.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, n∈ℕ, and v:Fin n→ℝ, define A(fp,n,v) by a left fold starting at a0=0 and setting a_(k+1)=fl_add(a_k,v(k)) for k=0,…,n−1; return a_n. For n=0 the result is zero.",
      "name": "Sequential rounded sum",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the rounded addition used in every sequential sum.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, selects its third field fl_add:ℝ→ℝ→ℝ, subject to the addition error axiom and fl_add(0,a)=a in D007.",
      "name": "Model addition projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses B^t=N, the exact-zero addition law, and all operation model equations.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "For an arbitrary sort α and a,b∈α, Eq(a,b) is the proposition that a and b are equal.",
      "name": "Equality",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Represents vector indices and recursive block indices. Since B>0 and N=B^t, the target's input index set is nonempty.",
      "id": "D015",
      "meaning": "For every n∈ℕ, Fin n is the type of natural numbers k with 0≤k<n, represented by a natural value and a proof of its strict upper bound.",
      "name": "Finite index type",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the exact sums in the target to range over every input index.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "For every n∈ℕ, supplies a finite enumeration of Fin n from the list 0,…,n−1, with no duplicates and with every element included.",
      "name": "Enumeration of finite indices",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the exact reference dot product and the exact sum of absolute products. These sums use ordinary real addition, not the rounded addition operation.",
      "id": "D017",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary types I and M, an additive commutative monoid structure on M, a finite set s⊆I, and f:I→M, returns ∑_{i∈s}f(i), implemented by mapping f over the underlying multiset and summing it. The empty sum is zero.",
      "name": "Finite exact sum",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes each target sum range over the whole of Fin N, without selecting a subset.",
      "id": "D018",
      "meaning": "For any type α equipped with a finite enumeration, returns the finite set containing every element of α.",
      "name": "Universal finite set",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves addition in the natural-number error index and block indices, and ordinary real addition in the model equations.",
      "id": "D019",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary types α,β,γ and a supplied heterogeneous addition structure HAdd α β γ, selects its binary operation α×β→γ. It imposes no algebraic laws by itself.",
      "name": "Addition operation selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves natural multiplication in t(B−1) and block offsets, and exact real multiplication in products, model equations, and the bound.",
      "id": "D020",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary types α,β,γ and a supplied HMul α β γ structure, selects its binary multiplication operation α×β→γ, without independently imposing algebraic laws.",
      "name": "Multiplication operation selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets B^t and the powers used in recursive vector lengths.",
      "id": "D021",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary base, exponent, and result types α,β,γ and an HPow α β γ structure, selects its exponentiation operation α×β→γ.",
      "name": "Power operation selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets B−1 using natural subtraction, and the dot-product error and coefficient denominator using real subtraction.",
      "id": "D022",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary types α,β,γ and an HSub α β γ structure, selects its subtraction operation α×β→γ.",
      "name": "Subtraction operation selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses the final real inequality, the nonnegativity of u, and the bounds |δ|≤u.",
      "id": "D023",
      "meaning": "For any type α with a supplied LE structure, selects its binary proposition-valued relation ≤. Its particular meaning comes from that structure.",
      "name": "Non-strict comparison selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses positivity of t and B, validity of finite indices, and the strict error-budget condition.",
      "id": "D024",
      "meaning": "For any type α with a supplied LT structure, selects its binary proposition-valued strict comparison relation <.",
      "name": "Strict comparison selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Uses natural-number monoid powers for the lengths B^t; in particular, the zeroth power is one.",
      "id": "D025",
      "meaning": "For any monoid M, equips M with exponentiation by n∈ℕ using the monoid's natural-power operation: a^0=1 and successive powers are repeated multiplication.",
      "name": "Natural powers in a monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Is the domain of t, B, N, the error index, and all index values. Negative depths and sizes are excluded.",
      "id": "D026",
      "meaning": "The type ℕ of natural numbers, including zero.",
      "name": "Natural numbers",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes B^t ordinary natural-number exponentiation.",
      "id": "D027",
      "meaning": "The multiplicative monoid structure on ℕ, inherited from its commutative monoid structure, with ordinary multiplication and identity one.",
      "name": "Natural multiplicative monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets numerical literals such as natural zero and one and real zero and one through their respective instances.",
      "id": "D028",

  "role": "blind-translation",
  "semantic_sha256": "93d32619dac894beb5b8ff69ea7810e49d893da3ef60b4f082a5f690344e4291",
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "For every arithmetic model fp of the type described by D002 and D007, with error parameter u.",
      "For every t,B,N∈ℕ, in that order.",
      "For every proof ht of 0<t, proof hB of 0<B, and equality hN:B^t=N.",
      "For every pair of real vectors x,y:Fin N→ℝ, after the size equality has been supplied.",
      "Assuming additionally ((t(B−1)+1):ℝ)u<1."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "Let m=t(B−1)+1∈ℕ. Then |C(fp,t,B,N,hN,x,y)−∑_{i=0}^{N−1}x_i y_i| ≤ [((m:ℝ)u)/(1−(m:ℝ)u)]·∑_{i=0}^{N−1}|x_i y_i|.",
      "The conclusion is an absolute forward-error bound against the exact real dot product. The scale is the sum of absolute exact products, equivalently the ℓ¹ norm of the componentwise product vector; it is not a bound relative to the absolute exact dot product."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "The model contains u∈ℝ with u≥0 and total real-valued operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div, and fl_sqrt.",
      "For every a∈ℝ, fl_add(0,a)=a.",
      "For each a,b∈ℝ and separately for addition, subtraction, and multiplication, there exists a real δ, possibly depending on the operation and a,b, with |δ|≤u such that the computed operation equals its exact real result multiplied by 1+δ.",
      "For every a,b∈ℝ with b≠0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_div(a,b)=(a/b)(1+δ).",
      "For every a∈ℝ with a≥0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_sqrt(a)=sqrt(a)(1+δ).",
      "The depth and branching factor satisfy t>0 and B>0; the vector length satisfies N=B^t.",
      "For m=t(B−1)+1, the additional hypothesis is (m:ℝ)u<1. Consequently m≥1, N≥1, u<1, and 1−(m:ℝ)u>0.",
      "No sign, nonzero-entry, representability, or normalization condition is imposed on x or y."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin n denotes {0,…,n−1}. The cast along hN:B^t=N preserves the underlying index.",
      "Natural subtraction is truncated at zero. In m=t(B−1)+1 it agrees with ordinary subtraction because B>0.",
      "Define A(fp,n,v) by a0=0 and a_(k+1)=fl_add(a_k,v(k)) for k=0,…,n−1, and return a_n.",
      "Define S(fp,B,0,v)=v(0). For d∈ℕ, define S(fp,B,d+1,v)=A(fp,B,j↦S(fp,B,d,i↦v(j·B^d+i))), with j∈Fin B and i∈Fin(B^d).",
      "Define C(fp,t,B,N,hN,x,y)=S(fp,B,t,i↦fl_mul(x(cast hN i),y(cast hN i))). The algorithm rounds each individual product, recursively processes contiguous blocks, and sequentially adds the B child results at each node.",
      "For n∈ℕ, γ_n=((n:ℝ)u)/(1−(n:ℝ)u), and admissibility at n means (n:ℝ)u<1.",
      "All arithmetic in the exact reference sum, the absolute values, and the bound is ordinary real arithmetic. For a∈ℝ, |a|=max(a,−a)."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every real-arithmetic model satisfying the supplied relative-error axioms and exact addition from zero, every positive natural depth t and positive natural branching factor B, every N=B^t, and all real vectors x and y of length N, compute each component product using the model's multiplication and sum those products by the specified recursive B-ary contiguous-block algorithm. If m=t(B−1)+1 satisfies mu<1, then the absolute difference between this computed value and the exact dot product is at most mu/(1−mu) times the sum of the absolute exact component products."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "For fixed parameters with mu≥1, the final implication has a false admissibility premise and gives no error guarantee. In particular, since m≥1, a model with u≥1 admits no target instance satisfying that premise.",

    "The hypotheses exclude t=0, B=0, and N=0. No empty-vector case occurs in the target, even though some supporting definitions accept zero sizes.",
    "B=1 is allowed. Then N=1 and m=1 for every positive t; every internal sum has one child and is exact by fl_add(0,a)=a, leaving only the individual multiplication error.",
    "When u=0, the bound is zero and the conclusion asserts exact equality. When every exact component product is zero, the right-hand side is also zero, so the conclusion again requires exact equality rather than becoming vacuous.",

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "Several generic declarations use the token LocalDef008 as a universe-level name, whereas D008 uses it as a real-valued model projection. These are different syntactic roles; the universe occurrences do not refer to the error parameter.",

  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the computed dot product whose absolute error is bounded.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, natural numbers t, B, N, equality hN: B^t = N, and functions x,y: Fin N → ℝ, form v(i) = fl_mul(x(cast hN i), y(cast hN i)) for i ∈ Fin(B^t), and return the recursive sum S(fp,B,t,v) defined in D005.",
      "name": "Computed hierarchical dot product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target universally quantifies over this type, so all the data and axioms specified by its constructor are implicit model assumptions.",

      "meaning": "The type of arithmetic models. Its supplied constructor D007 packages a nonnegative real error parameter, five real-valued arithmetic operations, exact addition from a zero accumulator, and relative-error axioms.",
      "name": "Arithmetic model type",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the bound's coefficient at n = t(B−1)+1.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, define γ_n = ((n:ℝ)u)/(1−(n:ℝ)u), where u is the model's error parameter. This is a total real expression in Lean; division by zero has value zero, although the target's hypothesis ensures a positive denominator.",
      "name": "Accumulated error coefficient",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target assumes this predicate at n = t(B−1)+1, ensuring the coefficient's denominator is positive.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n ∈ ℕ, the admissibility predicate is (n:ℝ)u < 1.",
      "name": "Error-budget admissibility",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the grouping and summation algorithm used after the individual rounded products.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and B,t ∈ ℕ, S(fp,B,t,·) maps real vectors of length B^t to ℝ.       "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the one rounded multiplication for each input pair.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For every model fp, selects its fifth field, fl_mul: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ. D007 requires that for all real a,b there exists δ with |δ|≤u and fl_mul(a,b)=ab(1+δ).",

      "status": "understood"

    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies all assumptions carried by fp. Addition, multiplication, nonnegativity of u, and exact zero-start addition govern the target algorithm; subtraction, division, and square root are additional model requirements even though the algorithm does not call them.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "Constructs a model from u∈ℝ with 0≤u; operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div: ℝ×ℝ→ℝ and fl_sqrt: ℝ→ℝ; the axiom ∀a∈ℝ, fl_add(0,a)=a; and the following axioms.     {

      "id": "D008",

    "binders": [
      "For every arithmetic model fp of the type described by D002 and D007, with error parameter u.",

      "Let m=t(B−1)+1∈ℕ. Then |C(fp,t,B,N,hN,x,y)−∑_{i=0}^{N−1}x_i y_i| ≤ [((m:ℝ)u)/(1−(m:ℝ)u)]·∑_{i=0}^{N−1}|x_i y_i|.",

      "The model contains u∈ℝ with u≥0 and total real-valued operations fl_add, fl_sub, fl_mul, fl_div, and fl_sqrt.",

      "For every a,b∈ℝ with b≠0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_div(a,b)=(a/b)(1+δ).",
      "For every a∈ℝ with a≥0, there exists δ∈ℝ with |δ|≤u and fl_sqrt(a)=sqrt(a)(1+δ).",

    "proposition_plain_english": "For every real-arithmetic model satisfying the supplied relative-error axioms and exact addition from zero, every positive natural depth t and positive natural branching factor B, every N=B^t, and all real vectors x and y of length N, compute each component product using the model's multiplication and sum those products by the specified recursive B-ary contiguous-block algorithm. If m=t(B−1)+1 satisfies mu<1, then the absolute difference between this computed value and the exact dot product is at most mu/(1−mu) times the sum of the absolute exact component products."
